newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro Disney again sees challenging 1997.
newsitem.headline: Euro Disney again sees challenging 1997.

text.p: Euro Disney SCA chairman Philippe Bourguignon said on Wednesday that this year presented a challenge for the Disneyland Paris theme park operator, reiterating a warning issued by the group in November.

"This is a satisfying performance demonstrating our ability to better exploit the potential of our low season," he said in a statement, commenting on the rise in 1996/97 first-quarter sales to 1.13 billion francs ($204 million) from 1.01 billion reported earlier.
"However, 1997 remains a challenging year with no price increases and higher financial charges," Bourguignon said.

"The decision to maintain fiscal 1997 prices at fiscal 1996 level, even though this might have a temporary detrimental impact on margins, is aimed at further consolidating and strengthening the position of Disneyland Paris," the statement said.

"As benefits of the 1994 financial restructuring continue to decline, lease and financial charges will increase by an estimated 200 million francs in fiscal year 1997 compared to fiscal 1996," it said.
Euro Disney issued a similar note of caution on November 19 when it reported its full-year 1995/96 results.

It said in November that although "public endorsement is definitely demonstrated" for the theme park outside Paris, "persistent weakness in the economy, constant pressure on our prices, and the strong increase in financial charges constitute several real challenges for the future, particularly in 1997".

The terms of the 1994 debt restructuring included a debt holiday which ended last year when financial charges were increased by 100 million francs. The sharpest increase -- 200 million -- occurs in the current year begun October 1, and a further 100 million franc increase goes into effect in 1997/98.

In reference to its sales results for the three months to December 31, 1996, Euro Disney said operating revenues for the theme park and hotels rose 11.4 percent to 1.12 billion francs from one billion in the first quarter of 1995/96.
"This increase in revenue was driven by both the growth in attendance and the per person average spent in the theme park and further increases in hotel occupancy," the statement said.
The share was trading up 0.75 franc, or 7.25 percent, at 11.10 francs at 1235 GMT.
